verse_text.translation: Don't be distressed, father. I will see this vow through. It was begun with determination, and determination is what carries it to the end.

reading: You feel determined to keep a resolve. Savitri tells her father-in-law that she began this vow with determination, and that same determination will carry her to the end. Let that steady resolve be the force moving you forward today, carrying you through to the finish.
meaning: Savitri speaks to her father-in-law Dyumatsena. She knows her husband Satyavan will die in three days. She has begun a severe three night vow without food. Dyumatsena is distressed by its harshness. Savitri tells him she started this with determination, and that same determination will carry her to the end. She means steady love and clear speech can face even death. Determination carries what fear would drop. You began a resolve with real determination. That same force can carry you through the hard middle, even when others doubt it.

verse_text.speaker: Krishna
verse_text.setting: Krishna on why people miss the divine and who turns to it.
verse_text.line: People turn to the divine in distress, in curiosity, in need, or in wisdom. All four are welcome.
verse_text.translation: Four kinds of good people worship me, Arjuna: the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the wise, best of the Bharatas.

reading: Krishna tells Arjuna that people turn toward the divine through distress, curiosity, need, or wisdom, and all four are welcome. Your curiosity places you among those who seek, and that seeking itself is counted as good. You do not have to arrive with answers; simply let this openness be the door you walk through today.
meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield. He has just said that the deluded do not turn to him. Now he names four kinds of good people who do. These are the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the wise. He says all four worship him. The point is that whatever brings a person to the search, whether trouble, curiosity, need, or wisdom, is welcome. Your curiosity is already a valid way in. You do not need to fix everything or arrive with answers before you begin.

verse_text.speaker: Krishna
verse_text.setting: Krishna on why people miss the divine and who turns to it.
verse_text.line: People turn to the divine in distress, in curiosity, in need, or in wisdom. All four are welcome.
verse_text.translation: Four kinds of good people worship me, Arjuna: the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the wise, best of the Bharatas.

reading: Krishna tells Arjuna that four kinds of people turn to the divine: those in distress, those seeking knowledge, those in need, and the wise. You are in a season of caring for your parents, and your curiosity is a genuine doorway, not a lesser one. The verse simply names curiosity as one of the ways people come, meeting you exactly where you are today.
meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield. He has just said that the deluded do not seek him. Now he names four kinds of good people who do. They are the distressed, those who seek knowledge, those who seek wealth, and the wise. He says all four kinds worship him. The verse proposes that whatever brings a person to the search is welcome. Distress, curiosity, need, and wisdom are all valid doors.

verse_text.speaker: Krishna
verse_text.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
verse_text.line: Dwell on something and you get attached; attachment becomes wanting, and blocked wanting turns into anger.
verse_text.translation: When a person dwells on objects, attachment to them is born. From attachment comes desire, and from desire, anger.

reading: You carry a feeling of anger right now. Krishna tells Arjuna that when someone dwells on objects, attachment is born, and from that attachment comes desire, which blocked turns into anger. This verse speaks to your anger today by tracing it back to something you kept turning over in your mind, until it became a need that could not rest. Notice where your mind keeps returning, and let that observation be your anchor today.
meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna after Arjuna asks what a person of steady wisdom looks like in speech, sitting and walking. Krishna explains that when a person dwells on objects, attachment to them is born. From that attachment comes desire, and from desire, anger. The verse traces how attention fixed on things hardens into craving, and blocked craving turns into wrath. Your anger today may have started long before it reached your chest, in a thought you kept turning over until it became a need. This verse points to that earlier stage.

verse_text.speaker: Krishna
verse_text.setting: Krishna on why people miss the divine and who turns to it.
verse_text.line: People turn to the divine in distress, in curiosity, in need, or in wisdom. All four are welcome.
verse_text.translation: Four kinds of good people worship me, Arjuna: the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the wise, best of the Bharatas.

reading: Krishna tells Arjuna that people turn to the divine in four ways: in distress, in curiosity, in need, or in wisdom. You are in your working years and feel curious, and that very curiosity places you among those who are welcomed. The verse simply names curiosity as a door that leads in, without asking you to fix anything first.
meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield. He has just said that the deluded do not turn to him. Now he names four kinds of good people who do. They are the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the wise. He says all four worship him. The idea is that whatever brings a person to the search is welcome. The door does not demand a pure motive first. Your curiosity is not a small thing. It places you in the same company as those who come seeking answers, and the text does not ask you to fix your life before you begin.

verse_text.speaker: Krishna
verse_text.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
verse_text.line: Heat and cold, pleasure and pain come and go. They don't last; learn to bear them.
verse_text.translation: Contact of the senses with their objects brings cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go and do not last. Bear them patiently, Arjuna.

reading: You feel anxious right now. Krishna tells Arjuna that contact between the senses and their objects brings cold and heat, pleasure and pain, and that they come and go without lasting. This means the discomfort you carry today is not permanent; it moves like weather. You might notice its edge without letting it define the whole day.
meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield. Arjuna is grieving and afraid. Krishna tells him that the true self is never born and never dies. Yet the body still meets cold and heat, pleasure and pain through the senses. These feelings come and go on their own. They do not last. Arjuna must learn to bear them without being swept away by either joy or grief. The anxious weight you carry right now moves like weather. It has not settled into who you are, and it will not stay fixed forever.

verse_text.speaker: Krishna
verse_text.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
verse_text.line: Without inner discipline there's no clarity; without clarity, no peace; and without peace, where is happiness?
verse_text.translation: For the undisciplined there is no understanding and no steady contemplation. Without contemplation there is no peace, and for the one without peace, where is happiness?

days.reading: Krishna tells Arjuna that without inner discipline there is no clarity, and without clarity no peace, so where is happiness? For you, the rush to book that tatkal ticket shows a mind chasing quick relief, yet the verse sees stress stealing happiness because a scattered mind cannot settle into contemplation first. The chain breaks at the mind, not at your effort.

verse_text.speaker: Krishna
verse_text.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on working in the world without being stained by it.
verse_text.line: Like a lotus leaf in water, do your work without letting the mess soak in.
verse_text.translation: One who acts offering all actions to the Supreme, giving up attachment, is not touched by wrong, as a lotus leaf is not wet by water.

days.reading: Krishna tells Arjuna to act like a lotus leaf in water, doing your work fully while letting the mess roll off. This means you can stay in the thick of deadlines and demands without letting the surrounding pressure soak into you. Let your tasks move through you, keeping your own surface dry as you go.

verse_text.speaker: Krishna
verse_text.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
verse_text.line: Rivers pour into the ocean and it stays full and still. Let desires enter you the same way.
verse_text.translation: As waters enter the ocean, which is ever being filled yet stays unmoved within its shores, so the one into whom all desires enter in the same way finds peace, not the one who craves desires.

days.reading: Krishna tells Arjuna that rivers keep pouring into the ocean, yet it stays full and still within its shores. Demands will keep coming at you, too. Peace belongs to the one who takes them in without being moved, like the ocean, rather than to the one who keeps craving relief from the timing pressure.

verse_text.speaker: Krishna
verse_text.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
verse_text.line: Moderate in food and rest, in work and play, in sleep and waking: that's how sorrow eases.
verse_text.translation: For one who is moderate in food and recreation, measured in effort at work, moderate in sleep and waking, yoga becomes the destroyer of sorrow.

days.reading: Krishna tells Arjuna to stay moderate in food, rest, work, play, sleep and waking, saying that this measured rhythm is what lets yoga destroy sorrow. You could try setting one fixed boundary today, like a set time to step away from the screen, so your body gets a small pause. This steadiness builds on the ocean’s stillness you read about yesterday, keeping pressure from filling every corner of your day.

verse_text.speaker: Krishna
verse_text.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on acting free of ego, like and dislike, in your own way.
verse_text.line: Hand your work to something higher, drop the 'mine' and the hoping, and act with the fever gone.
verse_text.translation: Surrendering all actions to me, with your mind on the inner self, free from hope and the sense of 'mine', fight with your fever gone.

days.reading: Krishna tells Arjuna to hand his work over and act with the fever gone, dropping the sense of 'mine' and anxious hoping. You could try offering one small task today to something larger than your worry, then do it without gripping the outcome. Let the heat drop as you move, rather than carrying it through the day.

story.title: Janaka on the palace roof
story.summary: Walking in his garden one spring, King Janaka overheard hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbed to his palace roof and questioned everything he had lived for. When his attendant came to call him to the day's work, he could have walked away from the throne. He didn't. He went back and did his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutched.
story.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

days.reading: King Janaka heard sages sing of the self, climbed to his palace roof, and questioned his whole life. When his attendant called him to work, he could have walked away from the throne, but he stayed and did his duties with a mind that no longer clutched. You, facing the pressure of tatkal ticket booking timing, can meet the day's demands without letting your mind tighten around them.

verse_text.speaker: Krishna
verse_text.setting: Krishna on why people miss the divine and who turns to it.
verse_text.line: People turn to the divine in distress, in curiosity, in need, or in wisdom. All four are welcome.
verse_text.translation: Four kinds of good people worship me, Arjuna: the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the wise, best of the Bharatas.

reading: Krishna tells Arjuna that four kinds of good people come to the divine: the distressed, the seeker of wealth, the seeker of knowledge, and the wise. Your curiosity places you among those welcomed here. You can step toward the Gita simply as a student drawn to know what it actually says, without any other reason.
meaning: Krishna speaks this to Arjuna on the battlefield. He has just said that the deluded and the wrongdoers do not turn to him. Now he names four kinds of good people who do. He says the distressed, the seeker of wealth, the seeker of knowledge, and the wise all worship him. He means that whatever brings a person to the search is welcome. The distressed come because they are hurting. The seeker of wealth comes because they need something. The seeker of knowledge comes because they want to know. Your curiosity is one of those four doors. You do not need to be in pain or looking for answers you cannot name yet. You can come simply as a student who wants to know what the text actually says.

verse_text.speaker: Lakshman
verse_text.setting: At Lake Pampa, Lakshman pulls Ram out of despair after Sita has been taken.
verse_text.line: There is no strength greater than enthusiasm. For the one who has it, nothing is out of reach.
verse_text.translation: Noble brother, enthusiasm is powerful; there is no strength greater than enthusiasm. For the person who has it, nothing in the world is out of reach.

reading: You carry a hopeful feeling as you step into a new beginning. Lakshmana tells Ram that enthusiasm is powerful, and for the one who has it, nothing in the world is out of reach. Let that resolve meet the concrete task ahead of you today, and let your first small act of will be enough.
meaning: At Lake Pampa in spring, Ram is drowning in grief after Sita has been taken. Every bird and mated deer reminds him of her, and the beauty around him only deepens his sorrow. Lakshman, Ram's younger brother, speaks to him directly. He says that enthusiasm is powerful, and there is no strength greater than it. For the person who has this energy, nothing in the world is out of reach. You are starting something new while holding onto hope. That same energy can carry you into the first concrete step of this beginning.

verse_text.speaker: Sanjaya
verse_text.setting: Sanjaya reports to the blind king the moment Arjuna gives up before the battle.
verse_text.line: Arjuna put down his bow and sat in the chariot, too overwhelmed to go on.
verse_text.translation: Sanjaya said: Having spoken this on the battlefield, Arjuna sank down on the seat of the chariot, letting fall his bow and arrows, his mind overwhelmed by grief.

reading: Between things, you feel lost. Sanjaya reports that Arjuna put down his bow and sat in the chariot, his mind overwhelmed by grief. This is the moment of laying everything down when you cannot go on. The story does not end there; the next verses move toward asking for help and finding a way forward.
meaning: Sanjaya speaks to the blind king Dhritarashtra from the battlefield. Arjuna has just argued that killing his own kin is a ruin no victory can mend, and he would rather die unarmed. Sanjaya reports that Arjuna sinks onto the chariot seat, drops his bow and arrows, and sits frozen, his mind overwhelmed by grief. You are between things and feel lost. This verse names the exact moment of laying everything down when you cannot go on, and it shows that the teaching begins right there.

verse_text.speaker: Krishna
verse_text.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the inner happiness of one who sees clearly.
verse_text.line: Happy within, at ease within, lit from within: that person finds lasting freedom.
verse_text.translation: One whose happiness is within, whose delight is within, and whose light is within, that yogi becomes one with Brahman and reaches the peace of Brahman.

reading: You carry a peaceful feeling while working, and Krishna says the one whose happiness, delight and light are all within becomes one with Brahman and reaches its peace. This points to a gladness that does not rely on what happens outside. You might notice where your ease comes from today, and rest in that inner source.
meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna while teaching the yoga of knowledge. He describes the wise person who sees clearly. Such a person keeps happiness, delight and light inside. That yogi becomes one with Brahman and reaches the peace of Brahman while still alive. Your peaceful feeling at work already hints at a gladness that does not lean on outside events. It points toward a steadiness you can rest in today.

verse_text.speaker: Krishna
verse_text.setting: Krishna on why people miss the divine and who turns to it.
verse_text.line: People turn to the divine in distress, in curiosity, in need, or in wisdom. All four are welcome.
verse_text.translation: Four kinds of good people worship me, Arjuna: the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the wise, best of the Bharatas.

reading: Krishna tells Arjuna that four kinds of good people turn to the divine: those in distress, those seeking knowledge, those in need, and the wise. Your curiosity places you among these welcomed seekers. The path is open to you exactly as you are, and your question today is a step onto it.
meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna after noting that the deluded do not turn to him. He names four kinds of good people who do worship him. These are the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the wise. The verse proposes that whatever brings a person to the search is welcome. It does not rank the motives or shut out those who come in pain or need. Your curiosity places you among these welcomed seekers. The path is open to you exactly as you are, and your question today is a step onto it.

verse_text.speaker: Bali
verse_text.setting: Bali, a king who has ruled for ages, sits by his window and wonders what it all adds up to.
verse_text.line: Day again, night again, the same tasks again, over and over. A thinking person feels mocked by it.
verse_text.translation: Again day, again night, again the same chain of tasks. Again and again: to a thinking person, I feel, this is a mockery.

reading: You feel restless while studying. The Yoga Vasishtha has Bali say that day and night bring the same chain of tasks again and again, and to a thinking person this feels like a mockery. That sense of repetition can sit with you today as a sign that your mind is awake to the loop, not as proof that your work is worthless. Let Bali’s window remind you to look for what your days are actually for.
meaning: King Bali has ruled the three worlds for ages. One day he sits by his window and notices that day follows night and the same tasks return without end. He speaks to himself and says that to a thinking person this endless round feels like a mockery. The verse proposes that when life feels like a loop, the work is not to add more tasks but to master the mind that runs the loop. Your studying feels like the same chain of tasks again and again, and that repetition is stirring a restlessness you cannot name yet.

verse_text.speaker: Krishna
verse_text.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on why even the fulfilled keep working for the world.
verse_text.line: Whatever a respected person does, others copy. The standard you set is the one people follow.
verse_text.translation: Whatever a great person does, others do the same. Whatever standard that person sets, the world follows.

reading: You feel inspired right now. Krishna tells Arjuna that whatever a respected person does, others copy, and the standard they set is the one the world follows. Your own conduct around your children and daily work quietly sets the tone for how they learn to handle success and pressure. Let your grounded effort be the quiet example they absorb.
meaning: Krishna speaks this to Arjuna on the battlefield. Arjuna has wondered why anyone should act when wisdom alone seems enough. Krishna answers that people look to those they respect and copy their actions. The standard a leading person sets becomes the rule for everyone else. Even someone who has no personal need still works, because others follow their example. Your children watch how you move through a win or a busy day. They absorb the standard you set without you having to name it.

verse_text.speaker: Krishna
verse_text.setting: Krishna on why people miss the divine and who turns to it.
verse_text.line: People turn to the divine in distress, in curiosity, in need, or in wisdom. All four are welcome.
verse_text.translation: Four kinds of good people worship me, Arjuna: the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the wise, best of the Bharatas.

reading: You feel curious right now. Krishna tells Arjuna that four kinds of good people turn to the divine: those in distress, those who seek knowledge, those who seek wealth, and the wise. Your curiosity places you among those welcome at the door, not outside it. Let this steady fact sit with you as you begin this week.
meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield. He has just said that deluded people do not turn to him. Now he names four kinds of good people who do. These are the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the wise. He says all four worship him. The verse proposes that whatever brings a person to the search is welcome. It does not demand a pure motive or a calm mind first. It simply counts the troubled, the curious, the needy, and the steady among those who come. You are standing at the start of something new with no crisis behind you. Your curiosity still counts as a valid reason to open this text.

verse_text.speaker: Arjuna
verse_text.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, who has collapsed in tears on the battlefield and refuses to fight.
verse_text.line: I'm confused about what's right. Tell me plainly what's best; I'm ready to learn.
verse_text.translation: My nature is stricken by weakness and my mind is confused about what is right. I ask you: tell me for certain what is best for me. I am your student; I have come to you, teach me.

days.reading: Arjuna tells Krishna his mind is confused about what is right and asks him to tell him plainly what is best, since he has come as a student ready to learn. Your curiosity opens the door to this same honest admission: when two choices both feel wrong, you can simply say you do not know which is best and ask for clarity. You do not have to defend a half-made choice; you can lay down the argument and let the teaching begin.

verse_text.speaker: Krishna
verse_text.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
verse_text.line: Heat and cold, pleasure and pain come and go. They don't last; learn to bear them.
verse_text.translation: Contact of the senses with their objects brings cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go and do not last. Bear them patiently, Arjuna.

days.reading: Krishna tells Arjuna that contact between the senses and their objects brings cold and heat, pleasure and pain, which come and go and do not last, so he must bear them patiently. For you, caught in a stressful stretch right now, this means the discomfort you feel is not permanent. Notice it as weather that begins and ends, and stand with it without adding panic or despair.

verse_text.speaker: Krishna
verse_text.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse_text.line: Your work is yours to do; the results are not yours to hold. Don't let that make you stop.
verse_text.translation: Your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit be your motive, and do not cling to doing nothing.

days.reading: Krishna tells Arjuna that your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits, and not to cling to inaction. Your curiosity brought you here, so let this ground you: give your full attention to the effort and craft you control, and let the outcome be what it will be.

verse_text.speaker: Krishna
verse_text.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
verse_text.line: Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.
verse_text.translation: Raise yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.

days.reading: Krishna tells Arjuna to raise himself by his own self and not let himself sink, because the self alone is the friend of the self and also its enemy. You could try speaking to yourself today with the same patience you would offer a friend checking into a Rishikesh hotel under 3000, simply noticing the next step without pushing harder.

verse_text.speaker: Krishna
verse_text.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the power of understanding to end confusion and guilt.
verse_text.line: Learn from those who have seen the truth: approach with humility, ask real questions, and serve.
verse_text.translation: Learn it by bowing down, by questioning, and by service. Those who are wise and have seen the truth will teach you that knowledge.

days.reading: Krishna tells Arjuna to learn from those who have seen the truth by bowing down, asking real questions, and serving. You could approach a trustworthy commentary or study circle with humility today, pose one genuine question about what you are curious about, and offer your attention in return. This keeps your inquiry grounded in actual understanding rather than drifting on its own.

story.title: Action with devotion: surrender
story.summary: Krishna urges Arjuna to offer all action, warns that ego will only trip him, tells him to reflect fully and then choose, and finally to take refuge in him alone and not grieve.
story.lesson: Reflect fully, choose freely, and set down the fear.

days.reading: After eighteen chapters, the Lord tells Arjuna he has shared the most secret knowledge and invites him to reflect fully and then do as he wishes. Because Arjuna is dear to him, the Lord adds that he should give up all other support and take refuge alone in him, promising to free him from all wrongs and bidding him not to grieve. This leaves the choice with you, pointing toward a decision you will make after weighing what you have heard.

Your curiosity is one of those welcomed doors. It can sit with your books today as a genuine step toward what you are exploring.

Distress, curiosity, need, and wisdom are all valid doors. Your curiosity sits in the same room as those who come because they are hurting or because they want something. It is not a lesser reason to be here.

verse_text.speaker: Rama
verse_text.setting: Young Rama, back from his travels, tells the sages in his father's court why nothing interests him.
verse_text.line: My heart feels heavy as stone, but I don't cry, because of what people would think.
verse_text.translation: Though my heart is packed tight with the stones of life's sorrows, I don't let my tears fall, only out of fear of what my own people would think.

reading: It sounds like you're carrying something very heavy right now.

verse_text.translation: Though my heart is packed tight with the stones of life's sorrows, I don't let my tears fall, only out of fear of what my own people would think.

verse_text.speaker: Angiras
verse_text.setting: The two birds, continued.
verse_text.line: The bird that eats grieves, lost in its helplessness. When it sees the calm one beside it, grief falls away.
verse_text.translation: On the same tree a person sits sunk, grieving, bewildered by his own helplessness. When he sees the other, the content lord, and his greatness, his sorrow leaves him.

verse_text.ref: Complete Works, Vol. 5, Epistles – First Series, CIII, p. 160
verse_text.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verse_text.setting: Letter from Belur, 18 May 1901, ill and grieving the sudden death of the Raja of Khetri.
verse_text.line: Yet I am sure to bob up soon and am waiting for the next turn.
verse_text.translation: The Raja of Khetri died from a fall a few months ago. So you see things are all gloomy with me just now, and my own health is wretched. Yet I am sure to bob up soon and am waiting for the next turn.

verse_text.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse_text.setting: Closing verse of the section on steadfastness.
verse_text.line: A cut tree grows back; the waning moon fills again. Remembering this, the wise do not despair.
verse_text.translation: A tree that is cut grows again; the waning moon waxes again in the world. Reflecting on this, the good are not tormented in this world.

verse_text.speaker: Vasishtha
verse_text.setting: Vasishtha on the fourth gatekeeper: good company (satsanga).
verse_text.line: Even at your lowest and most helpless, don't let go of good company.
verse_text.translation: Even when people fall into the hardest straits and feel helpless, they should not let go of good company, not even a little.

verse_text.speaker: Kabandha
verse_text.setting: Ram is lost and grieving; Kabandha tells him to seek Sugriva, who has also lost his wife and home.
verse_text.line: Find a friend who knows your kind of trouble. You won't get through this alone.
verse_text.translation: You must make him your friend, best of friends. Thinking it over, I see no success for you without it.

story.title: Kabandha: find a friend who understands
story.summary: Freed from a curse, the creature Kabandha tells the grieving brothers to seek out Sugriva, an exile who has also lost his wife and home. Only a friend in the same trouble, he says, can help them now.
story.lesson: When you are lost, look for someone who has been through the same thing.

verse_text.setting: Vibhishan, Ravana's good-hearted brother, describes his life in Ravana's court.
verse_text.line: I live here like the tongue among the teeth.
verse_text.translation: Son of the wind, hear how I live: like the poor tongue among the teeth. Friend, knowing me to be without support, will the Lord of the Sun dynasty ever show me grace?

verse_text.speaker: Vidura
verse_text.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verse_text.line: If you fear someone's anger or must tiptoe around them, they are not really your friend.
verse_text.translation: That is no friend whose anger you fear, or whom you must approach warily. A friend is one you can trust as you trust a father; the rest are mere acquaintances.

verse_text.speaker: Ram
verse_text.setting: Ram, having embraced Vibhishan, asks how he survived in Lanka.
verse_text.line: You lived among the cruel day and night. I know how you kept your goodness.
verse_text.translation: 'You lived day and night among the wicked; how did you keep your goodness, friend? I know all your ways: very wise in conduct, with no taste for wrong.'

verse_text.speaker: Seer
verse_text.setting: The creation story: last of all, dharma is made.
verse_text.line: Nothing is higher than what is right. With it the weak can face the strong. What is right is truth.
verse_text.translation: Still he did not flourish. So he created a higher form, dharma. Dharma is the power over power; nothing is higher than dharma. Through dharma even a weak man can stand up to a strong one, as with the help of a king. That dharma is truth. So people say of one who speaks truth, 'He speaks dharma,' and of one who speaks dharma, 'He speaks truth.' Both are the same.

verse_text.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse_text.setting: From the section on the wicked.
verse_text.line: Avoid a cruel person even if brilliant. A snake wearing a jewel still bites.
verse_text.translation: A wicked person should be avoided, even if adorned with learning. Is a snake any less frightening because it wears a jewel?

story.title: Shunahshepa, the son neither parent chose to keep
story.summary: A king needs a human substitute for a lost sacrifice and offers a fortune for a son. The father says: I will never sell my eldest. The mother says: the youngest is my darling, I cannot part with him. The middle boy hears both sentences and understands his place in the house. He says it himself: then the middle one is sold. Take me.
story.lesson: When those who should protect you do not, you may seek refuge elsewhere and ask plainly for what you need.
